title: Tracking a maximum through two transformations
caption: Track the key point. y = 3f(x − 1): inside the bracket moves x the opposite way (1 right), outside stretches y as written (× 3): (4, 6) → (5, 18). y = f(2x) − 5: inside halves x, outside moves down 5: (4, 6) → (2, 1).
alt: Graph of a curve y = f(x) with a maximum at (4, 6), and its transformations y = 3f(x − 1), with maximum at (5, 18), and y = f(2x) − 5, with maximum at (2, 1).
description: Three downward parabolas on one set of axes. The original curve y = f(x) has its maximum at (4, 6).
y = 3f(x − 1) is the same shape moved 1 to the right and stretched vertically by 3: it is three times as tall and its maximum is at (5, 18).
y = f(2x) − 5 is squeezed horizontally by a factor of 1/2 and moved down 5: it is narrower and its maximum is at (2, 1).
Arrows run from (4, 6) to each new maximum.

checks.name: f has its maximum at (4, 6), as in the worked example
